assets.title: Oncravia HCP detail aid - HORIZON-3 efficacy
assets.summary: Field-ready detail aid summarising the HORIZON-3 study design, progression-free survival results and important safety information for US healthcare professionals.

sections.heading: Study design
sections.body: HORIZON-3 was a randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial in 612 adults with previously treated advanced solid tumours. Participants received Oncravia plus standard therapy or standard therapy alone. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent review. This is synthetic demonstration content.

sections.heading: HORIZON-3 progression-free survival
sections.body: In the HORIZON-3 trial, Oncravia plus standard therapy increased median progression-free survival to 11.8 months versus 7.6 months with standard therapy alone (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.54-0.86). The separation of the Kaplan-Meier curves was observed from the first scheduled assessment.

sections.heading: Important safety information
sections.body: The most common adverse reactions (>=20%) with Oncravia in the HORIZON-3 safety population were fatigue, nausea and rash. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 18% of participants receiving Oncravia and required monitoring in the clinical setting. Refer to the fictional prescribing information for the complete safety profile. This is synthetic demonstration content and not medical advice.

sections.heading: Patient support
sections.body: The Oncravia Nurse Navigator program provides US patients with optional one-to-one support, including help understanding insurance and treatment logistics. The program does not provide clinical advice and does not replace the treating team.

sections.heading: What is Oncravia?
sections.body: Oncravia is a fictional medicine studied in adults with advanced solid tumours in the HORIZON-3 trial. Your care team can explain whether a treatment is appropriate for your individual situation. This page is synthetic demonstration content.

sections.heading: What the HORIZON-3 study showed
sections.body: In the HORIZON-3 trial, Oncravia plus standard therapy increased median progression-free survival to 11.8 months versus 7.6 months with standard therapy alone (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.54-0.86). Progression-free survival is the time a person lives without the cancer getting worse. Individual results vary.

sections.heading: Important safety information
sections.body: The most common adverse reactions (>=20%) with Oncravia in the HORIZON-3 safety population were fatigue, nausea and rash. Tell your care team about any side effects you experience. This is fictional demonstration content and must not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional.

sections.heading: Nurse Navigator support
sections.body: The Oncravia Nurse Navigator program provides US patients with optional one-to-one support, including help understanding insurance and treatment logistics. A navigator can help you prepare questions for your care team, but does not provide medical advice.

assets.title: Aerivant HCP detail aid - AIRWAY-2 exacerbations
assets.summary: UK HCP detail aid covering AIRWAY-2 exacerbation and patient-reported outcome results, with safety information and fair balance.

sections.heading: AIRWAY-2 study design
sections.body: AIRWAY-2 was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in 1,204 adults with moderate-to-severe asthma. The primary endpoint was the annualized rate of moderate-to-severe exacerbations over 52 weeks. This is synthetic demonstration content.

sections.heading: Exacerbation results
sections.body: In AIRWAY-2, Aerivant reduced the annualized rate of moderate-to-severe exacerbations by 34% versus placebo (rate ratio 0.66; 95% CI 0.52-0.84). The effect was consistent across the predefined subgroups.

sections.heading: Patient-reported outcomes
sections.body: In AIRWAY-2, patients reported a 6.1-point improvement in the St George's Respiratory Questionnaire total score at week 52 versus 2.4 points with placebo. The St George's Respiratory Questionnaire measures respiratory health status.

sections.heading: Important safety information
sections.body: The most common adverse reactions reported with Aerivant in AIRWAY-2 were nasopharyngitis, headache and cough. Refer to the fictional summary of product characteristics for the complete safety profile. Synthetic demonstration content, not medical advice.
